 GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers first. After all speakers in the Chambers have spoken,
the Presiding Officer will call upon those participating via zoom or teleconference.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, virtually, email, phone call, mail and any other method which may become
available. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such times when a State of
Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email at
yglaze@sogate.org.

DEVELOPMENT  AND  DIRECTOR  OF PUBLIC  WORKS  TO  EXTEND  EXPIRED  PLAN
CHECK  AND  PERMIT  APPROV  ALS  ISSUED  BY THE  CITY  BETWEEN  MARCH  1, 2020,
AND  DECEMBER  31, 2021, FOR  A PERIOD  NOT  TO  EXCEED  UP TO AND  INCLUDING
JUNE  30, 2023

PURPOSE:  The  proposed  Resolution  will  allow  the Director  of Community  Development  and
Director  of Public  Works  to extend  expired  plan check  and permit  approvals  for a period  up to and
including  June 30, 2023.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Adopting  a Resolution  authorizing  the Director  of Commiu'iity  Development  and Director
  of Public  Works  to extend  expired  plan  check  and permit  approvals  issued  by the City
  during  the period  from  March  1, 2020,  through  and including  December  31, 2021,  for a
  period  not to exceed  up to and including  June 30, 2023;  or
  b.  Maintaining  status  quo  and  requiring  applicants  with  expired  plan  check  and  permit
  approvals  to comply  with  current  codes, submit  a new application,  and pay applicable  fees.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  If  the  City  Council  adopts  the  proposed  Resolution,  the  new  Platu'iing
Application,  Building  Permit,  and Building  Inspection  Fees would  be waived  for each application
that receives  an extension.

ANALYSIS:  City  staff issued a number  of plan check  and permit  approvals  during  the period  from
March  1, 2020 through  and including  December  31, 2022.  Under  the South  Gate Municipal  Code,
City  staff is not authorized  to extend  the expiration  dates for those plan checks  and permit  approvals
which  remain  outstanding

Granting  the Director  of Community  Development  and the Director  of Public  Works  the respective
authority  to extend  expired  plan checks  and permit  approvals  would  allow  COVID  impacted  projects
to move  forward  through  the development  process  without  paying  additional  fees, and allowing  such
project  to  move  forward  without  "restarting  the  clock"  and  being  subjected  to  additional
requirements  caused by COVID-related  impacts.  These expired  projects  generally  consist  of simple
improvements  ranging  from  mechanical,  electrical,  plumbing  to  new  ADUs,  multiple  family

  16
 residential  units,  and  large  non-residential  developments.  Staff  recognizes  that  some  delays  on
projects  may  have  been  due  to financial  hardships  resulting  from  the  pandemic  and/or,  lack  of
staffing  to process  applications  in normal  time  frames.

Most  applicants  have  continued  where  they  le:tt off  during  the  height  of  the  pandemic,  having
resubmitted  plans,  paid  applicable  fees  and  redesigned  their  projects  to  meet  today's  codes.
However,  there  are a handful  of applicants  who  have  asked  that the City  take into  consideration  the
recent  pandemic  and the significant  hardship,  financial  and/or  personal,  that occurs  in their  situation
by paying  additional  fees  and/or  redoing  plans  again.  In these  cases,  the applicants  indicate  they
cannot  move  forward  due to the hardship  and require  more  time.  If approved,  the Resolution  would
grant  City  staff  the ability  to provide  additional  time  extension.

BACKGROUND:  Current  zoning  regulations  preclude  staff  from  granting  approval  and permit
extensions  or waiving  development  fees.  The  City  of South  Gate's  Municipal  Code,  unlike  many
other  cities,  does not include  language  that  allows  staff  to extend  Planning  approval  up to a certain
period  of time,  when  an applicant  applies  for a time  extension.  Additionally,  staff  does not have  the
authority  to waive  fees without  Council  approval.

To date,  to maintain  consistency  in the application  of the City's  current  regulations,  all applicants
with  expired  approvals  and  permits  are required  to reapply,  comply  with  current  codes,  and pay
applicable  fees.  Currently,  the  Building  &  Safety  Division  has no expired  building  permits.  The
Building  Official  has the authority  to extend  building  pernnits  on a six-month  increment,  given  the
applicant  is making  progress.  The  Building  Official  has  exercised  this  authority  throughout  the
pandemic.  The  Planning  Division  on the  other  hand,  has several  approvals  that  are expired  or are
about  to expire,  but are within  the time  period  stipulated  above.  Approving  the proposed  Resolution
would  provide  significant  relief  to many  of these  applicants.

Based  on the situations  summarized  above,  staff  is requesting  that the City  Council  consider  one of
two  options:  1) adopt  the proposed  Resolution  to provide  relief  to eligible  applicants;  or 2) maintain
status  quo. Approving  the Resolution  would  allow  applicants  to resubmit  previously  approved  plans
without  waiting  months  for approval,  paying  additional  fees,  and redesigning  the project  to comply
with  today's  code.  Maintaining  status  quo  would  require  applicants  to reapply  and go through  the
development  approval  process  again,  pay  fees and comply  with  today's  code.

SUBJECT:  AGREEMENT  WITH  THE SOUTH  GATE  CHAMBER  OF COMMERCE  FOR
PROMOTION  OF COMMUNITY  ACTIVITIES

PURPOSE: The proposed Agreement will provide financial assistance to the South Gate Chamber
of Commerce ("Chamber")  to advertise and promote the residential, commercial, and industrial
advantages of the City, and the benefits of living in or locating business or industry within the City
of South Gate during Fiscal Year 2022/2023 through Fiscal Year 2024/2025.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City Council will  consider:
  a.  Approving an Agreement with the South Gate Chamber of Commerce for promotion of
  community activities in Fiscal Years 2022/2023, 2023/24 and 2024/25 in the amount not
  to exceed $50,000 each Fiscal Year; and
  b.  Authorizing  the Mayor to execute the Agreement  in a form acceptable to the City Attorney.

FISCAL IMPACT:  Funds in the amount of $50,000 were included in the FY 2022/23 budget  in
Account Number 100-601-42-6308 (General Fund - Community Development Administration  -
Civic Engagement). If approved, staff will budget $50,000 in FY 2023/24 and FY 2024/25.

ANALYSIS:  The approval of the proposed Agreement will enable the Chamber to continue
advertising and promoting activities that support the goals of encouraging economic development
and workforce development, as well as improving cornrnunications and civic engagement in the City
of South Gate.

BACKGROUND:  Over the past several years, the City has contracted on a yearly basis with the
Chamber to undertake business promotion activities. Currently, the Chamber is requesting funding
from the City in the amount not to exceed $50,000 for FY 2022/23, $50,000 for FY 2023/24, and
$50,000 for FY 2024/25 to continue providing services to the South Gate residents and business
community. This funding request is the same amount provided by the City in previous fiscal years.

Continued Activities  and Services
Using the requested funding, the Chamber will continue to disseminate information to the public
about the benefits of locating a business in the City; serve as an informational bureau; maintain an

  20
 office  within  the  City  which  is accessible  to the public;  publicize  City-sponsored  activities  and
functions;  advertise  and promote  the commercial  expansion  and development  of the City;  and work
with  the City,  county  and other  public  and private  agencies  to obtain  appropriate  information  and

June 23, 2022,  in the City  Clerk's  Office  for  the Thermoplastic  Striping  of Streets  Citywide

(Project)  is a part  of the  Capital  Improvement  Program.  The  total  budget  appropriation  was
$280,000  to restripe  the crosswalks  at 12 locations  near elementary  schools  citywide.  The scope
of the Project  included  the installation  of ADA  access ramps  and the restoration  of the asphalt
pavement  prior  to installing  the thermoplastic  continental  design  crosswalks.  The  Project  was
advertised  for construction  in the local  press and trade publications.  On June 23, 2022,  the City
Clerk's  Office  received  three bids all of which  were higher  than the engineer's  estimate  and well
over the Project  budget  (See Attachment  A).  The table  below  provides  a summary  of the bids
received.  Staff  is recommending  that all bids be rejected.  Under  the South  Gate Municipal  Code
Section  1.54.475  (Rejection  of Bids),  the City  has the right  to reject  construction  bids at its sole
discretion,  by City  Council  action.  This right  was further  stipulated  in the Notice  of Inviting  Bids

BACKGROUND

  Gambling in California. The California Constitution and state law limit gambling in
California.  For example,  state law bans sports betting,  roulette,  and games with dice (such as
craps). However,  it allows  some gambling.  This includes:

  *  State Lottery.  About  23,000  stores in all 58 counties  sell state lottery  games. Lottery
  sales-after  prizes and operation costs-support  education.  About  $1.9 billion  in
  lottery revenue  supported education last year.

  *  Cardrooms.  Currently,  84 cardrooms  in 32 counties  can offer certain  card games
  (such as poker).  Cardrooms  pay state and local fees and taxes. For example,
  cardrooms  pay the state around $24 million  each year (annually)  generally  for
  regulatory costs. Cardrooms  also pay around $100 million  each year to the cities they
  are located in.

  *  Horse  Racing  Betting.  Four privately  operated racetracks  as well as 29 fairs, publicly
  operated racetracks,  and other facilities  in 17 counties  offer betting  on horse racing.
  The horse racing  industiy  pays state and local fees and taxes. Last year, the industry
  paid the state around $18 million  in fees primarily  for state regulatory  costs.

  *  Tribal  Casinos.  Tribes  operate 66 casinos in 28 counties  rinder specific  agreements
  between  certain tribes and the state (discussed  below).  These casinos offer slot
  machines,  lottery  games, and card games on tribal  lands. Last year, tribes paid around
  $65 million  to support  state regulation  and gambling  addiction  programs.  Tribes  also
  pay tens of millions  of dollars  to local governments  each year. Additionally,  tribes
  operating larger casinos pay nearly $150 million each year to tribes that either do not
  operate casinos or have less than 350 slot machines.

  Tribal-State  Compacts.  Native  American  tribes have certain rights under federal  law to
govern  themselves,  such as certain rights to offer gambling.  This means that the state generally

  Proposition  26 would  impact  both state and local government  revenues  and costs. The actual
size of these effects,  however,  is uncertain  and would  depend on how the proposition  is
interpreted  and implemented.  For example,  it is unclear  if tribal-state  compacts  changed to allow
for sports betting  would  require  additional  payments  to local governments.  The fiscal effects
would also depend on the number of people who choose to make sports bets and how often the
new  civil enforcement method is used.

  Itxeeased  State Revetxues.  Proposition  26 would  increase state revenues  from racetrack  and
tribal  sports betting  payments  as well as civil  penalties.  The size of this increase  is uncertain,  but
could reach tens of millions  of dollars  annually.  Some of this revenue would  be new.  For
example,  the state currently  does not receive  any share of illegal  sports bets. This means the state
would  receive new revenue  when people make sports bets legally  rather than illegally.  However,
some of this revenue  would  not be new. For example,  the state currently  receives revenue  when
people spend money  on certain things,  such as lottery  games or shopping.  This means the state
might  not receive  new revenue when people  spend less on those things so they could make sports
bets.

  Some of the increased  revenue would  go into the CSWF.  This would  result in a higher
minimum  amount  of spending  on K-12  schools and community  colleges  than would  otherwise  be
required.  About  40 percent  of CSWF  money  would  likely  be used to meet this higher minimum
spending  amount.  The remaining  60 percent would  be used for sports betting  and gambling-

CITY OF SOUTH GATE
  REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MINUTES
  TUESDAY, AUGUST 23, 2022
CALL TO ORDER  Al Rios, Mayor called a Regular City Council Meeting to order at 6:56
  p.m.

INVOCATION  Pastor Lawrence Doss, Community of Faith Bible Church

PLEDGE OF
ALLEGIANCE  Wendy O'Kelly, Deputy Director of Administrative Services

ROLL CALL  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk

PRESENT  Mayor Al Rios, Vice Mayor Maria del Pilar Avalos, Council Member
  Maria Davila, Council Member Denise Diaz, and Council Member Gil
  Hurtado; City Manager Chris Jeffers, City Attorney Counsel Raul F.
  Salinas

1
PERSONNEL RECRUITMENT
& SELECTION  The City Council considered the list of new and promotional full-time
  employees hired or promoted during July 2022.

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE - NON-AGENDA
ITEMS  Jesus Miranda questioned why Council made the decision to hire a new
  trash hauler. He was happy with Waste Management and hopes that he
  gets better service and prices with the new trash hauler.

  Mario Dominguez would like a phone meeting with the Vice Mayor and
  Councilwoman Diaz next week regarding some projects he would like to
  ask the Council Members to incorporate into the city's master plan.
  Explains that he is unable to do that if the council members are unaware of
  what those projects are and what they entail, how he is going to fund them
  and feasibility.

  Liz Ruiz inquired about the tree planting that was previously proposed.
  She talks about other projects that are planned that include planting trees
  like the Long Beach Conservation Core.

  Virginia Johnson, South Gate resident asked if the city clerk can mention
  at 6:30 when it is completely silent that council is in closed session. So,
  people don't think their computers are not working. Also, would like to
  know if they could get the agendas to their emails because the website is
  not user friendly. She gave a shoutout to Cassie Garage now called Rosa
  Trucking Auto Repair, because every morning there is an employee out
  there sweeping the corner and provides the address. Wishes all businesses
  would do the same. She thanks her neighbor Andrea Paulino for going out
  daily and calling the city on messes that are made like graffiti, trash, and
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF AUGUST 23, 2022

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE - NON-AGENDA
ITEMS CONT'D  other items. Talks about all the illegal handmade signs that are put on
  gates and fences, would be nice if the city department can be more active
  in this area. Explains that from 2003 - 2015 there were many times that a
  lot of people were speaking on one item that the mayor would request to
  take 1-2 minutes. Says this practice was great but it was stopped.

  Thomas Buckley stated that Thursday, August 25th is supposed to be a
  Brown Act meeting and would like more information. He also asked if the
  meeting will be available on zoom. Thanks, the Chief of Police Darren
  Arakawa for everything he does and the department. Explains that there
  was a disturbing video of a dog being beaten and a lot of residence are
  wondering if there are any updates to this situation. To the nominees he
  says he is glad that there is not a lot of old school attacks going on and is
  glad that they are not attacking people, he is hopeful that they can start off
  on the right foot and without any attacks.

  Frank Rivera commented regarding water conservation rules. He proposes
  a suggestion and one of them is to produce grant funding to get one of
  those rebates that are being given out to water districts explains that the
  Metropolitan District pays out two dollars per square foot for residents to
  replace their lawn. He understands that this is not possible for a lot of
  residents but encourages the council to investigate the grants opportunities
  so that they can be able to supplement some of these programs to give the
  community an opportunity to make sustainable changes in terms of water
  conservation. This is a continuing issue that has been going on for some
  time and would like to find a long-term solution for these problems.

  Andrea Paulino addresses the new nominees she would like to know if
  everyone is going to go on social media to get the opportunity to see what
  is being said. Says it would be nice to hear from all the nominees on sites
  that everyone is welcomed.

  Jovanna Laborin thanked South Gate Police Department and the parks
  staff for all the great work they have been doing at the park. They have
  been seeing less graffiti and less activity, they don't see fires anymore.

  Candice Esquivel asked if it is possible to have speed traps on Tweedy
  Boulevard by the park. She understands that the police cannot stay in one
  area all the time, but it is very dangerous for pedestrians to cross on cross
  walks that do not have light. She explained one situation that happened
  yesterday while she was driving down Tweedy Boulevard.

  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk has an email she would like to read. The
  resident's name is Claudia Rivera she has been a resident all her life and
  has just found out that Robert Montalvo is running for office and has
  given a very deceiving candidate statement. The resident explains that he

  Page 2 of 9
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF AUGUST 23, 2022

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE - NON-AGENDA
ITEMS CONT'D  is using a scare tactic by talking about the dirty water issue that the city
  cleared up. The resident thanks the city for clearing up the issue and
  providing information. Asks if someone from Public Works can address
  this tonight and would like Mr. Montalvo to explain how he plans to keep
  the water safe.

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS  Chris Jeffers, City Manager speaks a little bit regarding the trees and says
  he is not aware of any projects now and passes it on to Arturo Cervantes to
  further answer the question.

  Arturo Cervantes, Director of Public Works says this is something that he
  has gotten a lot of questions a couple of months ago. He did meet with the
  tree people from Parks & Recreation along with Public Works, they had a
  kickoff meeting to discuss the grants that was received to plant around
  16,000 trees in South Gate and Cudahy. They applied for the grant and
  tried to get an agreement to come forward and get it approved by the
  Council. He doesn't have a more recent update, but he will have one very
  soon and will provide everyone with that.

  Chris Jeffers explains that there is a different procession for those that are
  participating by phone and those on zoom. Sometimes they have difficulty
  hearing through the phone because of connection issues so it does makes
  things difficult sometimes to hear everything residents are saying.

  Mayor Rios agrees and says that maybe they could do something to
  improve the hearing in the chambers.

  Council Member Davila asks what streets the crosswalks were.

  Chris Jeffers says that the Chief has written it down. He continues
  answering the questions regarding the trash contract. He doesn't want to
  take comments away from the Council, but he will remind the residents
  that it is about an 8 month process they went through, they had two
  meetings where they discussed the RFP and the contents of the request for
  proposal that had been sent out. He continues to go through the process
  they went through before picking the new trash hauler. Reminds residents
  that Council Member Hurtado recused himself from the process. Also
  goes over some of the changes like the amount that residents will now be
  paying compared with the previous hauler and discusses some of the new
  mandates that they must meet when it comes to trash haulers. He will be
  happy to answer any questions residents have regarding this subject.

  Council Member Davila agrees with City Manager and explains that UWS
  had cheaper services which gave a better price to residents which made it
  the best hauler. It also included all the state mandated services.

  Page 3 of 9
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF AUGUST 23, 2022
REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS
CONT'D  Mayor Rios mentions that UWS is a local company and Waste
  Management did a good job. Explains that with UWS they got a better
  deal for less money, and he explains other reason why he believed that
  UWS was the best choice.

  City Manager mentions the Brown Act meeting, says that the flyer is on
  the city website and reminds the residents when and where it will be held
  for those who want to join the meeting. He also goes over what the
  meeting will be about and that it will be a power point presentation.

  Arturo Cervantes, Director of Public Works commented on the water
  conservation comments. He explains that the city has an ordinance that has
  a permanent water consumption, that is the goal, and the residents must
  help achieve that goal. The additional measure that is in effect that has had
  a big effect is the designated days when they are required to water their
  lawns. Explains they have done a lot of initial outreaches and they will
  continue to do so with regards to water conservation. Regarding the
  comment about the dirty water, there are still state and federal
  requirements that must be fulfilled. Since 2021 the city has flushed lots of
  times, he is unsure how many times they have done. Explains that there is
  a city-wide flushing and then a smaller flushing in different areas that are
  routine that the city does to ensure that the water quality is good. Says the
  city is applying for a grant, they were selected, it is up to 3 million dollars
  for water replacement.

  Meredith Elguira, Director of Community Development has nothing to
  report.

  Steve Costley, Interim Director of Parks & Recreation stated receiving a
  call from Janice Hahn's office to do a food distribution at the South Gate
  Park. Explains that they did several in the park during the pandemic and
  they would like to bring them back, it will be held at the park on August
  31' from 9 o'clock to 12 o'clock noon. The LA Food bank will be coming
  as well to supply fruits and vegetables. The Police Department will take
  care of the traffic, Parks and Recs will oversee the set up. He invites
  everyone to be a part of it and explains they have not received the flyers
  yet but once they get the flyers, they will post it on social media.

  Vice Mayor Avalos asks if it is possible to do it on the weekend because
  the families work, and they could have the opportunity to go get some
  food.

  Steve Costly explains that the date was given to them by the Office of
  Janice Hahn, but he will ask if they can get it changed.

  Arturo Cervantes, Director of Public Works has nothing to report.

  Page 4 of 9
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF AUGUST 23, 2022

  REPORTS AND COMMENTS
  FROM CITY OFFICIALS

I  CONT'D  Kris Ryan, Director of Administrative Services explains that they will
  have a meeting next Monday on the proposed budget along with
  department presentation. That will be Monday starting at 5pm in the
  Council Chambers, they will be having zoom, and later this week they will
  be publishing the agenda. They will also extend the presentation until
  Tuesday at 5pm where they will ask the council to approve the budget and
  get any feedback regarding the budget.

  Chief of Police Arakawa has nothing to report.

  Chris Jeffers, City Manager has nothing to report.

  Raul F. Salinas, City Attorney has nothing to report.

  Greg Martinez, City Treasurer has nothing to report.

  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk named the qualified candidates that are running
  for Council and other elected city officials. She will be scheduling a Meet
  and Greet to introduce the candidates and the Department Heads.

  Council Member Hurtado reminds everyone that school is back in session
  and safety is a top priority. Council Member Hurtado says that the Chief is

I  giving a lot of citations to drivers, but he believes that more needs to be
  done, says they are doing a great job and recommends a couple of corners
  to keep an eye on. He talks about some of the things going on right now,
  such as the Inflation Reduction Act and the cancelation of up to 10,000
  dollars in student loans.

  Councilwoman Davila has nothing to report.

  Councilwoman Diaz addressed a couple of things, would like the City
  Treasurer to echo the same sentiments and talks about finding a solution to
  the homeless problem. Talks about the Inclusive Housing Act that passed
  and the rent control cap that other cities had. She wants to make sure that
  the residents stay housed. The other thing she wants to talk about is the
  encampments, she doesn't want to criminalize being homeless, but she
  expresses her concern when encampments are close to schools because
  they are unaware of people's backgrounds. She wants to investigate this,
  make the families feel safe and have an item on the agenda to discuss. A
  few weeks ago, she attended the screening of "If I go will they miss me," it
  was a great turn out rate.

  Vice Mayor Avalos congratulates the qualified candidates and wishes

I  them luck. She had the pleasure last week of going with the Mayor and the
  Chief to talk to Jackie Goldberg to make sure certain issues are being
  addressed. She indicated she is willing to work with us regarding

  Page 5 of 9
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF AUGUST 23, 2022

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS
CONT'D  renaming of the field for Henry C. Gonzalez. She also met with Mr.
  DeWitt, and they talked about the things he and Henry did to get that
  property. Vice Mayor Avalos brought up an issue to the City Manager
  regarding the street vendors on State Street, hopes they could investigate
  that because they are having a difficult time servicing their clients because
  they are unable to find parking. Explains that they want a 20 min parking
  spot so that they could get their customers to come pick-up and then leave.
  Finds it interesting that LAUSD is having a mobile library and South Gate
  is one of the cities that was chosen, they will be coming into the
  community to do read along with the children. Regarding Mr. Dominguez,
  she would reach out to him, apologizes because school is back in session
  making everything hectic.

  Mayor Rios would like to follow up on Councilwoman Diaz concern with
  the homelessness around the schools and green spaces. He explains that it
  has been a common theme the last couple of months and talks about an LA
  county ordinance regarding homelessness but still thinks that it is a topic
  that should be up for discussion and supports Councilwoman Diaz that
  they move forward with looking at things the city can do.

  Chris Jeffers, City Manager explains that he did receive the email from
  Councilwoman Diaz about the article and he forwarded it to Raul's office.
  He has looked at it and is preparing a memo for them to review soon.

  Mayor Rios thanked City Manager and stated the superintendent was in
  the city. He visited some homes to find out why some kids were not
  returning to school; Mayor Rios had the opportunity to spend some time
  with him and visit the schools in the area as well. He explains the
  importance of the visit and explains some of the commitments they have
  made to the schools in the city, and they had a meeting with other
  Southeast High School leaders to see how they could improve the schools
  in the area. He also met with Jackie Goldberg and discussed public safety
  along with the Chief. The one important take away is that it looks like
  Zipperman says they will fill some of the positions that were lost. The
  other thing is that the Aztec football team permit was still under
  consideration but now it is not, and he hopes that they could move forward
  in getting a field. Says they will also see about the naming of the football
  field and talks about the next step. The last thing he would like to say is
  that back to school has caused a lot of traffic and is worried about
  emergency vehicles being able to come in and asks the chief to investigate
  that.

  Chief Arakawa explains that it is normal for the streets to be congested
  like this the first few weeks and it is nothing new. It is just a matter of
  informing the parents of what they can and can't do. They have already
  teamed up with some of the parents from some of the Eastside schools,

  Page 6 of 9
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF AUGUST 23, 2022

  REPORTS AND COMMENTS

I  FROM CITY OFFICIALS
  CONT'D  they are addressing some of the issues they are getting emails about.
  Explains that it is a slow issue because there are thousands of parents, but
  they are getting out there and trying to make things as safe as possible.

  Councilwoman Diaz says this is an issue every school year and it is
  addressed during the School Safety Meetings. She understands that Chief
  Arakawa does a good job along with the rest of the PD staff trying to keep
  the traffic under control.

  Mayor Rios explains that he does see crossing guards at the school, but
  they need a little more help getting traffic under control. Thanks everyone
  for their comments and concerns.
